page: Microsoft Azure E192ids_v6 is an isolated, memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Edsv6 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 192 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 1832.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 9.54 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of 11339 GB of bundled local disk capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations place the multi-core performance of this instance in the top tier. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test achieved a score of 158923.19, and the Geekbench multi-core score reached 21589.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached bandwidth measured at 12329.57 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 187.08 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate by comparison, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1929.19 and Geekbench single-core scoring 2155.0, both falling into average to strong categories. Database operations performed exceptionally well, with PassMark database operations scoring 35481.69 and Redis SET operations reaching 179.31 million operations per second.

The E192ids_v6 offers high resource density, combining massive memory capacity with a substantial local storage footprint. This profile is suitable for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, and data-heavy applications. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it demonstrates strong CPU-based LLM inference capabilities, such as processing 240.31 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. The instance is best suited for large relational databases, in-memory analytics, enterprise-grade web serving, and complex software compilation tasks.

It features 192 dedicated vCPUs (96 physical cores) running at 4.2 GHz, 1832.0 GB of RAM, and 11339 GB of local storage. The instance lacks GPU accelerators but delivers top-tier multi-core and memory performance.
